availability.note: Leapmotor AU B05 page names Style and Design LR with 'Request a Quote'/'Book a Test Drive' and an active $35,990 drive-away offer (1 Jul-31 Dec, while stocks last); offers page (https://www.leapmotor.net/en-au/offers) runs the same campaign. Leapmotor AU has no public configurator with prices. Chasing Cars (3 Jul 2026) says orders open; CarExpert review (22 Oct 2026) confirms both grades on sale.

listPrice.note: CarExpert review (22 Oct 2026): Style $35,888 before on-road costs. Same figure in CarExpert price news (4 Jul 2026, https://www.carexpert.com.au/car-news/2026-leapmotor-b05-price-and-specs) and Chasing Cars (3 Jul 2026, https://www.chasingcars.com.au/news/new-car-prices/leapmotor-b05-2026-rear-wheel-drive-hatchback-priced-from-35888-to-rival-mg4-and-model-3-rwd/: 'All prices listed are before on-road costs'). No manufacturer list price is published; Leapmotor prints only the drive-away campaign. Victorian drive-away via calc/onroad.js: $38,354. The current $35,990 d/a Lightning Yellow offer (to 31 Dec 2026, incl. 12 months rego, CTP, stamp duty, dealer delivery) sits below that, i.e. a discounted campaign, not a mislabelled list.

batteryKwh.note: usable, EV Database (European car, same 56.2 kWh LFP pack Leapmotor AU prints unlabelled in the MY26 buyer's guide https://www.leapmotor.net/docs/default-source/b05-library/b05-buyersguide-my26-v101.pdf). CarExpert spec page labels 56.2 'useable', which matches the nominal figure and is treated as gross, as on leapmotor-b10.

rangeKm.note: Leapmotor AU MY26 buyer's guide (June 2026): EV range up to 401 km (WLTP combined); no NEDC figure published for the B05. Both grades on 19-inch alloys (225/45R19 front, 235/45R19 rear), so the 'up to' figure is the local wheel. EV Database agrees.

consumptionKwhPer100km.note: Leapmotor AU buyer's guide: energy consumption 158 Wh/km WLTP. Usable/range gives 13.7; the gap is charging loss, inside the 25% tolerance.

bootLitresSeatsUp.note: Leapmotor AU buyer's guide: rear cargo volume behind 2nd row 357 L. CarExpert spec page (https://www.carexpert.com.au/leapmotor/b05/2026-style-hatchback-rwd-electric-jskawmwm20260701) labels 357 L 'rear seat up; to lower window', i.e. to the cargo cover. The 345 L in European sources (EV Database, Auto Express, and the FAQ on Leapmotor's AU page) is a different measurement, not used. No frunk.

bootLitresSeatsDown.note: Leapmotor AU buyer's guide: behind 1st row 1,205 L. European sources give 1,400 L (different method).

seats.note: CarExpert spec: 2 front + 3 rear; EV Database 5.

towKg.note: CarsGuide 2026 table: Style and Design LR 0 kg braked. Leapmotor AU buyer's guide gives no towing figure. EV Database 0 kg; Auto Express (UK, https://www.autoexpress.co.uk/leapmotor/b05/369770/new-leapmotor-b05-2026-review-lack-thrills-dents-its-appeal) says the B05 'is not capable of towing'. CarExpert spec pages list 750 kg braked and 750 kg unbraked (equal figures, likely a database default); not used. Matches leapmotor-b10 electric (0 kg).

warrantyYears.note: Buyer's guide: vehicle warranty 6 years/150,000 km, high-voltage battery 8 years/160,000 km, 8 years roadside and capped-price servicing. Unconditional.

insuranceAnnual.note: anchored to mg-4-essence-64 ($37,458, $1,450), byd-dolphin-premium ($36,990, $1,400), gac-aion-ut-luxury ($35,990, $1,450) and leapmotor-b10-style ($37,888, $1,550); a step above the hatch rivals for 160 kW RWD performance, below the B10 SUV

depreciationCurve.note: Leapmotor brand curve [1, 0.72, 0.59, 0.5, 0.43, 0.37], as held on leapmotor-b10 and leapmotor-c10, per the one-curve-per-brand convention. Below mainstream for thin local volume, no resale history, and drive-away campaigning from launch.
